title: Regiment and Clock
premise: In 1913, apprentice clockmaker Lena Whitlock is hired to restore the observatory's failing master clock, the mechanism that keeps every railway, factory, and church bell in the valley honest. When the army requisitions the town for war mobilization, they also seize the registrar's ledger containing every resident's name — including forged ones Lena's late father used to hide their true origins. To protect a family of refugees sheltering in her workshop, Lena must finish repairing the clock before the army synchronizes its schedules to it, while deciding whether loyalty to those who saved her matters more than the truth that could destroy them. She completes the repair, but at the final moment alters the clock's chime sequence into a coded warning that gives the family one night's head start — and confesses everything to the young officer who has come to trust her.
about_author: Ulyana Iversen is the pen name of a former museum conservator who spent a decade restoring mechanical clocks in Central European collections. Her fiction is drawn from the marginalia she found penciled inside clock cases — names, dates, and small confessions left by the hands that kept time running.

chapters.title: The Escapement
chapters.summary: Lena arrives at the hillside observatory to assess the master clock, finding it deliberately sabotaged rather than merely worn. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: cautious curiosity hardening into unease as she realizes someone wanted time in this town to stop.

chapters.title: Names in the Ledger
chapters.summary: In town, Lena visits the registrar to copy parts records and glimpses the great ledger of residents' names — and the page bearing her father's careful forgeries. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: dread; the past she buried is a document with an official seal.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Grey-uniformed officers occupy the town square, posting orders and seizing the ledger 'for mobilization audit.' The observatory is claimed as a signal station. POV: alternating Lena and Lieutenant Brandt, the conscientious officer overseeing the seizure. Emotional beat: the ordinary world tilts; both feel the trap closing.

chapters.title: Workshop Hours
chapters.summary: Lena works by lamplight on the escapement while hiding the Voss family, refugees whose names appear in the seized ledger under false entries her father made years ago. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: tenderness and fear braided together; busy hands as refuge.

chapters.title: The Officer's Watch
chapters.summary: Brandt brings his broken pocket watch to Lena's workshop, unaware of the family behind the partition wall. A wary conversation about duty and fathers begins an unlikely rapport. POV: Brandt. Emotional beat: loneliness meeting kinship across an impossible line.

chapters.title: Synchronization Order
chapters.summary: Brandt delivers news: once repaired, the master clock will anchor the army's departure timetables — and any household whose ledger entry fails verification will be detained before the trains leave. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: the stakes fuse; finishing the work now endangers everyone she shelters.

chapters.title: Sabotage Reconsidered
chapters.summary: Lena discovers who damaged the clock: old Horst, the observatory's dying keeper, who slowed time hoping to delay the war's arrival. He teaches her the chime-sequence cams, calling it 'the clock's second voice.' POV: Lena. Emotional beat: grief becoming inheritance; she receives the tool she'll need.

chapters.title: Verification Day
chapters.summary: Officers go door to door checking ledger names against faces. The Vosses hide in the workshop cellar as Brandt, sent to inspect Lena's premises, stands close enough to hear breathing through the floor. He says nothing — but he knows. POV: Brandt. Emotional beat: silent complicity; loyalty quietly shifts sides.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Climax. On completion night, Lena finishes the restoration, then recuts the chime cams so the midnight bells ring a pattern the Vosses will recognize as flight instructions — buying them hours before the timetable locks. Brandt arrives mid-act and must choose; he watches, then helps her set the last pin. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into resolve; truth spoken aloud between them.

chapters.title: Keeping Time
chapters.summary: The trains depart on schedule; the Vosses are gone over the pass. Lena confesses her forgery to Brandt, who files a report omitting what he cannot unknow. The master clock runs true above a changed town, and Lena takes up Horst's post as its keeper. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — belonging earned not by hiding the truth but by paying its cost.
